title: [0.98a] PatchLib
author: Lukas04
contentHtml:
PatchLib is a library mod that enables bytecode patching at runtime for starsector.
To install it, simply drop the mod in to your mods folder like other mods. Only install it if a mod requires it.




[Incompatibility Warning] This mod is currently not compatible with mods that upgrade the games java version from 17 to 25+ (like Mikohime 28).
However, the "Fast Rendering" mod fixes the issue that causes this incompatibility, so you can use that to prevent this issue.


For mod authors

PatchLib allows modifying and redirecting existing code at runtime. This means that it can change the behaviour of starsector and mod code.
If you come from games with C# modding, it can be somewhat compared to the Harmony library, or Mixins if you are more involved with minecraft modding.
This capability is useful, as you may often find yourself in situations where you need a hook to modify some game behaviour, but there just is no API for it.

PatchLib provides an annotation based API for other mods. With it you register your patches and patch handlers.
The example patch below hooks in to the addPostDescriptionSection and applyEffectsBeforeShipCreation methods from the Automated hullmod.
Both hooks insert code after the original methods ran, allowing us to add additional effects and tooltip descriptions.



Unlike other ways to replace code, this doesnt require fully overwriting the plugin, which now allows multiple mods to insert their changes in to a single hullmod.
There are also countless examples where the game does not provide any way to replace the code, but with PatchLib you can insert hooks in to most of them.

Wiki

PatchLib has its own wiki which explains and documents most of the details that you will need.
The wiki asumes that you have basic starsector modding and programming knowledge.
https://github.com/Lukas22041/PatchLib/wiki

When should you use PatchLib?

PatchLib has a lot of utility, but it should generaly be the last resort to choose as your solution.
The game has a relatively vast API, which allows quite a lot of things if you stay within the scope of the base game.
Patches should only be used if there are no other options, or if the other options require much worse solutions than a patch.

AI generated content disclaimer

The libraries code has been co-developed with the help of Claude Code and the models Claude Fable 5, Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Opus 5.5.
The generated pieces of code have been heavily tested and are understood decently well by me. No visual assets were created with generative AI.
All documentation is written by hand, but has had grammatical corrections applied through AI tools.
